note: Written from the ORBIT README's assembly order and this model's measured positions. The pictures are Fusion's own, taken from camera_carrier v10. Physical fit against the real camera is not verified yet.

steps.title: What goes together
text: Printed: head sled, stand, tilt knob, rear gate, lens ring, pivot bolt.

Bought: one nylon friction washer, about 0.5 mm thick, M4 inside diameter, and either one M4 hex nut (7 mm across the flats) or the printed threaded nut from the model (m4_nut), which has an M4x0.7 thread opened 0.15 mm for printing.
The camera in its original UC-346 front and back case.
The Fusion model also lays out the fit coupon, the reference board and the tilt gauge off to one side. They are tools, not part of the stack.
steps.check: Do the fit coupon and the carrier test first. Assemble with the camera out until the stack moves smoothly.

images.caption: Finished, from the front

images.alt: The finished assembly seen from the back and the left
images.caption: Finished, from the back

steps.title: Bolt into the sled
text: Push the pivot bolt into the sled's inboard pivot counterbore, thread end pointing outward.
The head seats about 58.35 mm along the pivot axis and sits below the sled's side edge.
steps.check: The head is recessed and does not touch the case slot.

images.alt: The head sled with the pivot bolt sticking out of its side
images.caption: Bolt through the sled

images.alt: The head sled from the front with the bolt along the pivot axis
images.caption: From the front

steps.title: Washer on the boss
text: Slide the nylon washer over the bolt until it rests on the sled's boss.
It sits in the 0.55 mm gap between the boss and the stand arm's inner face.
steps.check: The washer lies flat. A different thickness changes the gap, so measure it first.

images.alt: The sled with the washer on the bolt
images.caption: Washer on the bolt

images.alt: The sled from the front with the washer against the boss
images.caption: From the front

steps.title: Stand arm on the bolt
text: Hold the sled against the stand's arm and feed the bolt through the arm's pivot hole.
The arm's inner face meets the washer.
steps.check: The sled hangs free of the stand's base and swings without scraping.

images.alt: The sled mounted on the stand arm
images.caption: Sled on the stand

images.alt: The stand from the front with the sled on its arm
images.caption: From the front

steps.title: Nut into the knob, knob on the bolt
text: Press the nut (bought or printed) into the tilt knob's hex socket (about 7.15 mm across the flats, 3.45 mm deep). A dab of glue or a piece of tape holds it if it is loose.
Put the knob on the bolt from outside the arm. The bolt tip ends inside the nut socket, about 43.85 mm along the axis.
steps.check: Tighten by hand only. The knob sets friction, not a click-stop, and PETG cracks if you overtighten.

images.alt: The stand with the orange tilt knob on the arm
images.caption: Knob on

images.alt: The stand from the front with the knob at the far end of the bolt
images.caption: From the front

steps.title: Camera case into the sled
text: With the camera out, slide the assembled UC-346 case in from the rear (the ribbon-exit side), under the left and right lips, until it reaches the front stops.
Do not force a case that is out of tolerance. Stop and measure it.
steps.check: The case slides in by hand and sits against the stops.

images.alt: The sled with the case seated in it, from the front
images.caption: Case seated, front

images.alt: The sled with the case seated, from the back
images.caption: Case seated, back

steps.title: Rear gate
text: Fit the rear gate. It is the keeper that holds the case in the sled.
steps.check: The gate clears the ribbon and can be taken off again for service.

images.alt: The sled with the grey rear gate fitted
images.caption: Gate fitted

steps.title: Lens ring
text: Put the lens ring on the front, decorative dots facing outward.
steps.check: The lens sees clear through the ring.

images.alt: The finished head with the orange lens ring
images.caption: Ring on

images.alt: The finished head from the back
images.caption: From the back

steps.title: Try the tilt
text: Turn the knob loose, tilt the head through its range, then tighten it just enough to hold the angle against the cable's pull.
The tilt gauge is a flat printed protractor with a tick every few degrees. Use it to read the angle. How it is held against the head is not in the model yet.
steps.check: Note anything that binds or touches the lens or ribbon.

images.alt: The flat half-round tilt gauge with its tick marks
images.caption: Tilt gauge
